fields.meta_title: Plumber Landing Page That Books Service Calls | Emergent
fields.meta_description: A plumber landing page that books calls into arrival windows. See four plumbing examples, from drain clogs to sewer scopes. Free to start.
fields.h1: Build a Plumber Landing Page That Books Calls by Arrival Window
fields.hero_description: Build a plumber landing page where customers book an arrival window, and every service call lands in a database you own.
fields.features_heading: What Gets a Plumber Booked From the Page
fields.features_subheading: Customers book when they can see when the van will arrive. Emergent builds these six parts of the page from one prompt.
fields.feature_1:
Arrival windows the customer picks

Show the day's 2-hour windows as buttons, such as 8-10 or 1-3, and hide any window the schedule has filled. The customer leaves the page with a time, not a wait for a callback.
fields.feature_2:
A separate path for a leak in progress

Ask whether water is leaking right now, before any calendar. A yes puts the dispatch number on screen as a button, because that caller needs a person today, not a slot tomorrow.
fields.feature_3:
Access notes next to the address

Ask for the gate code and where the water shutoff sits in the same step as the street address. The technician reads both on the drive over and starts work instead of calling ahead.
fields.feature_4:
A booking email to the dispatcher

Email each new booking to the person who runs the board, with the window and the address in the subject line. The office inbox gets a copy for days the dispatcher is out.
fields.feature_5:
Reviews that name the repair

Quote customers in their own words about the job you did, such as a toilet reset before guests arrived. A line about one real repair reads as true in a way a row of stars does not.
fields.feature_6:
The code, exported to your GitHub

Paid plans export the full code of the page to your GitHub repository. A developer you hire later starts from the working page, and every booking stays in a database you own.

fields.tab_content_1:
Three calls per window, and then it closes

Fernhallow Plumbing sells time on its page, not a callback. The customer picks one of four 2-hour arrival windows: 8-10, 10-12, 1-3, or 3-5. Each window holds 3 calls, and a full one drops off the page, leaving only times the crew can keep. Thursday has 11 calls booked: 8-10, 10-12, and 1-3 are full, and 3-5 has 2.
fields.tab_content_2:
Main line clogs go to Tobin and the jetter: 8 of 34

The first thing Mossgate Plumbing's drain page asks is which drain is backed up, with four choices: Kitchen sink, Shower, Toilet, and Main line. A Main line call goes to Tobin Ashgrove, who runs the jetter truck, and the other three go to the service techs. This week 34 drain calls came in: 8 for Tobin and 26 for the techs.
fields.tab_content_3:
No calendar for a leak in progress, just the phone

Quarry Lane Plumbing's page opens with one Yes or No question about a leak in progress. A Yes shows the dispatch number as a button and emails Selma Brightwater, the on-call plumber, with the address. A No opens the booking calendar. This month 52 visitors answered: 9 picked Yes and 43 picked No.
fields.tab_content_4:
Tight closings, 5 of 18, go to Odile ahead of the schedule

Harrow Creek Plumbing books sewer scopes for home buyers and asks for the closing date along with the address. A booking with a closing inside 7 days emails Odile Fenwright, the office manager, before it reaches the schedule. This month 18 scopes were booked, and 5 had a closing inside 7 days.

fields.howto_title: How to Create a Plumber Landing Page
fields.howto_description: Seven steps to a plumber landing page that fills arrival windows and sends each call to the plumber who takes it.
fields.howto_step_1_title: 01 Set the size of each arrival window
fields.howto_step_3_title: 03 Give each service its own page
fields.howto_step_4_title: 04 Ask what the tech needs at the door
fields.howto_step_1_des: Decide how many calls a 2-hour window can hold before you write any copy. A fixed cap gives the customer a time the crew can keep, and it gives dispatch a day that fits the vans on the road.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Put the leak question above everything else on the page. A Yes needs the phone number on screen right away, and a No can go on to the calendar. That one question keeps a flooded basement out of next week's 1-3 window.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Point the drain ad at the drain page and the sewer scope ad at the scope page. A buyer who searched for a sewer scope before closing sees those words in the headline, along with a field for the closing date.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Add a field for the gate code and one for where the water shutoff is, next to the address. Leave out anything the tech will learn in the first minute on site, because every extra field is one more reason to stop typing.
fields.howto_step_5_title: 05 Name who takes each kind of call
fields.howto_step_5_des: List every job in your prompt next to the person who handles it. Main lines go to the jetter truck, closings inside 7 days to the office manager, and leaks in progress to the on-call plumber. Emergent builds the routing from that list.
fields.howto_step_6_title: 06 Read the confirmation as a customer
fields.howto_step_6_des: After the booking, the page should repeat the window and the address back to the customer. Add one line on who calls if the tech is running late, written in words the office will keep to.
fields.howto_step_7_title: 07 Book a test call in every window
fields.howto_step_7_des: Book the windows yourself until one fills, and check that it drops off the page. Send one call of each type and confirm each email reaches the right person and each booking shows up as a row before the first ad runs.

faq_plan.q: What is a plumber landing page?
faq_plan.a: A plumber landing page is a single page with one job: turning the people an ad or a search sends to it into booked service calls. It names the problem it fixes, shows the phone number, and lets the customer pick an arrival window, with no menu leading anywhere else.

faq_plan.q: How do I create a plumber landing page?
faq_plan.a: Describe your arrival windows and which plumber handles which job to Emergent's AI landing page builder. It builds the page and the booking form, with a database behind them. Then book a test call in each window from your phone before you publish.

faq_plan.q: What should a plumber landing page ask before booking a call?
faq_plan.a: Ask only what decides who goes and what they bring: the problem, the address, and the window. A drain call needs to know which drain; a water heater call needs tank or tankless, and gas or electric. Each answer saves to its own column in a database you own.

faq_plan.q: Can one plumber landing page also take heating calls?
faq_plan.a: It can, if the first question splits the trades: water and drains on one side, heating and cooling on the other, each with its own choices and windows. If heating work brings in a large share of your calls, give it a separate HVAC landing page, so the ad and the headline say the same thing.

faq_plan.q: How many arrival windows should a plumber landing page offer?
faq_plan.a: Offer the windows your crew already works to. Four 2-hour windows between 8 and 5, each capped at the calls one van can finish in that time, is a simple place to start. On a day a tech is out, lower the cap instead of removing the window.

faq_plan.q: What should a plumber landing page show after hours?
faq_plan.a: Show the after-hours number and say which problems it is for, such as an active leak or no water at all. Everything else can book the next open window in the morning. When the on-call schedule changes, describe the change to Emergent in a sentence and it updates the page.

faq_plan.q: Should a plumber landing page show photos of real jobs?
faq_plan.a: Yes. Use photos your techs took on the job, and caption each with what was fixed and the town it was in. A roofing landing page does this with finished roofs; for a plumber, a cleared cleanout or a new shutoff valve under a sink tells the same story.

faq_plan.q: Can a plumber landing page send bookings to my dispatch software?
faq_plan.a: Yes, if the dispatch software has an API. Apps built with Emergent connect to any tool with an API, so each booking can create a job on the dispatch board and also save as a row in your own database. Send one test booking through before the first ad runs.

faq_plan.q: Is a plumber landing page template enough, or should I build one from a prompt?
faq_plan.a: A template gives you the layout, but it knows nothing about your windows or who takes which call. Building from a prompt starts with those rules. Emergent builds the page and its booking logic from one plain-English description, and the free tier covers building and publishing.

faq_plan.q: Should bathroom remodel requests go on a plumber landing page?
faq_plan.a: Give them their own page. A remodel request needs a budget range and a site visit, which reads more like a contractor landing page than a service call. Keep the plumber page for work that fits an arrival window and a van.

plan.angle: Searchers for plumber landing page get agency guides, design galleries and template pins that show how a plumbing page looks, never how it books a service call or what happens to the booking after the customer taps the button. This page shows four plumber landing pages built around the service call (arrival windows that close when full, a drain form that sends main line clogs to the jetter truck, a page that asks whether water is leaking right now before it offers a calendar, a sewer scope page for home buyers that flags closings inside 7 days), each with the form, the routing and the saved booking behind it, then gives the build steps a plumber needs. It makes no licensing, plumbing code, permit, insurance, pricing or state-specific claims. HVAC, roofing and contractor pages are siblings and stay out of the headings.
